chunks: 10 - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-A'mash, from Abaya ibn Rib'i, from Abdullah ibn Abbas who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey to the heavens, Gabriel brought him to a river called 'The Light' (al-Nur), and it is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'He created the darknesses and the light.' When he arrived with him at that river, Gabriel (peace be upon him) said to him: O Muhammad! Cross over with the blessing of Allah, for Allah has illuminated your sight and extended your view ahead. Indeed, this is a river that no one has ever crossed — not an Angel of Proximity nor a commissioned prophet — except that I immerse myself in it every day, then I come out and shake my wings. There is not a single drop that falls from my wings except that...
He created the darknesses and the light (Quran 6:1)

When he reached that river, Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: O Muhammad, cross over with the blessing of Allah, for Allah has illuminated your sight and extended the path before you. This is a river that no one has ever crossed -- neither a near-stationed angel nor a sent prophet -- except that I have one immersion in it each day; then I come out from it and shake my wings. There is not a drop that falls from my wings except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, creates from it a near-stationed angel having twenty thousand faces and forty thousand tongues, each tongue speaking in a language that the other tongue does not understand.

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) crossed over until he reached the veils -- and the veils were five hundred veils, and from one veil to the next was a journey of five hundred years. Then Jibril said: Go forward, O Muhammad! The Prophet said to him: O Jibril, why will you not be with me? He said: It is not permitted for me to pass beyond this place. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went forward as Allah willed until he heard what the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, said: I am the Praised (al-Mahmud) and you are Muhammad -- I derived your name from My Name.

Whoever maintains ties with you, I will maintain ties with him; and whoever severs ties with you, I will cut him off. Descend to My servants and inform them of My honor toward you -- that I have never sent a prophet without appointing for him a minister, and that you are My Messenger and Ali is your minister.

So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) descended but was averse to telling the people anything, out of fear that they would accuse him -- for they had only recently left the age of ignorance. Six days passed thus, and then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed:
"Perhaps you will forsake some of what is revealed to you, and your breast will become straitened because of it" (Quran 11:12)
The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) bore that until the eighth day came, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed upon him:
"O Messenger, convey what was revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people" (Quran 5:67)

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: A threat following a warning -- I shall indeed carry out the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For if they accuse me and deny me, that is easier for me than to suffer the most painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. He then said: Jibril greeted Ali with the title Commander of the Believers. Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Messenger of Allah, I hear the speech but I do not perceive the vision. He replied: O Ali, this is Jibril who has come to me from my Lord to confirm what He had promised me.

Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) directed man by man from his companions until they all greeted him with the title Commander of the Believers. Then he said: O Bilal, proclaim among the people that tomorrow no one should remain behind except the ill, but should go out to Ghadir Khumm. When the next day came, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) went out with all his companions, praised Allah and exalted Him, then said: O People, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent me to you with a message, but I felt constrained by it, fearing that you would accuse me and deny me, until Allah revealed to me warning after warning, and your denial of me is easier for me than the punishment of Allah upon me. Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, took me on the night journey and made me hear, and said: O Muhammad, I am the Praised (al-Mahmud) and you are Muhammad -- I derived your name from My Name. Whoever maintains ties with you, I will maintain ties with him; and whoever severs ties with you, I will cut him off. Descend to My servants and inform them of My honor toward you, and that I have never sent a prophet without appointing for him a minister, and that you are My Messenger and Ali is your minister. Then he (may Allah bless him and his family) took both hands of Ali ibn Abi Talib and raised them until the people saw the whiteness of their armpits -- something never seen before. Then he said: O People, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is my master, and I am the master of the Believers. Whoever I was his master, then Ali is his master. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be enemy to whoever is enemy to him; and support whoever supports him, and forsake whoever forsakes him.

The people saw the whiteness of their armpits -- something that had never been seen before. Then he said: O People, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is my master, and I am the master of the Believers. Whoever I was his master, Ali is his master. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be enemy to whoever is enemy to him; and support whoever supports him, and forsake whoever forsakes him. The doubters, the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a spreading disease said: We disown before Allah a statement that is not obligatory, and we are not satisfied that Ali should be his minister -- this is tribalism on his part. But Salman, al-Miqdad, Abu Dhar and Ammar ibn Yasir said: By Allah, we did not leave that ground until this verse was revealed:
"Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you, and I have approved Islam as your religion" (Quran 5:3)

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) repeated that three times, then said: "Indeed, the perfection of the religion, the completion of the favor, and the approval of the Lord is by My sending to you, with the guardianship after me, to Ali ibn Abi Talib."

key_terms.إمرة المؤمنين: The command over the believers; Amir al-Mu'minin, the title given to Ali by Gabriel and then by the Prophet
key_terms.الإسراء: The Night Journey (Isra); the miraculous nocturnal journey of the Prophet to the heavens
key_terms.الحجب: The Veils; cosmic barriers in the heavens separating realms, each spanning 500 years of travel
key_terms.المحمود: The Praiseworthy; one of God's attributes from which the Prophet's name Muhammad is said to be derived
key_terms.الوزير: The Vizier; the appointed successor/minister; used here for Ali as the Prophet's designated deputy
key_terms.الولاية: Wilaya; the spiritual authority, guardianship, and right of succession invested in Ali after the Prophet
key_terms.غدير خم: Ghadir Khumm; the pool/pond at Khumm where the Prophet made his historic proclamation on 18 Dhul-Hijja 10 AH
key_terms.ملك مقرب: Angel of Proximity; the highest class of angels close to God
key_terms.من كنت مولاه فعلي مولاه: The Hadith al-Ghadir; 'Whoever I am his master, Ali is his master' — the central declaration of Ghadir
key_terms.نهر النور: The River of Light; a celestial river described in this hadith as the source of Angels of Proximity

ai.seo_question: What happened during the Prophet's Night Journey regarding the appointment of Ali ibn Abi Talib at Ghadir Khumm?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of al-Saduq, narrated through Ibn Abbas, recounts two interconnected events: the Night Journey (Isra) during which Gabriel brought the Prophet to a celestial River of Light and the Prophet received the Divine command to declare Ali ibn Abi Talib as his vizier, and the subsequent event of Ghadir Khumm where the Prophet publicly proclaimed Ali's Wilaya. The hadith contextualizes the Ghadir proclamation within the Night Journey experience, emphasizing that God Himself ordained Ali's appointment and that the Prophet had been commanded to convey this message — with Quranic verses 5:67 and 11:12 serving as divine pressure to overcome the Prophet's reluctance. This account provides a cosmological-theological foundation for the Shia doctrine of Imamate and represents one of the key narrations linking the Isra with Ghadir.
